newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Aircraft says SAS order two planes.
newsitem.headline: Saab Aircraft says SAS order two planes.

text.p: Saab Aircraft AB said on Thursday that SAS Commuter had ordered two new Saab 2000 aircraft to be delivered in early 1998 and based at Stockholm's Arlanda airport.
This order for the Saab 2000 high speed turboprops brings the Scandinavian airline's total to six, Saab Aircraft said in a statement.
SAS Commuter, the Swedish domestic network arm of the airline, put the first of its initial order for four into service six months ago and had an option for a further two of the 47-seat aircraft.
The aircraft have replaced Fokker F-28 and McDonnell-Douglas MD80 jets on domestic as well as international routes, the statement said.

"Traffic boosts following the changevoer include a 30 percent traffic growth on the Stockholm-Tampere (Finland) route and a 30 percent increase in passengers between Stockholm and Kalmar (Sweden)," Saab Aircraft said.
